connectionConfigSchema.title: FB_CUSTOM_AUDIENCE rETL connection config
connectionConfigSchema.description: Per-connection destination config for a VDM v2 rETL connection, as accepted in `destinationConfig` on POST /v2/retl-connections. Keys match what the transformer reads off connection.config.destination in processRecordInputsV2. isValueBasedAudience is absent on purpose: integrations-info /setup derives it from identifierMappings, and config-backend derives it the same way, so a caller cannot set it. syncMode, schemaVersion, eventType, identifierMappings and fieldMappings are written by config-backend. Keys the dashboard writes but nothing reads are not accepted: a caller copying a dashboard-made connection has to drop them, and config-backend has to strip them on read so an import does not carry them into a spec that then fails validation. For this destination that key is `subtype`, which the webapp writes on every connection (lower-case t). The transformer reads `subType` and writes data_source.sub_type from it, so a lower-case `subtype` never reaches Meta; the ~397 connections already carrying it send no sub_type at all. Correcting those rows changes what they deliver, so it needs its own decision rather than a spelling this schema accepts. No default is declared anywhere in this file: config-backend applies none, and a default here would become a written-out field in a generated IaC spec and then a permanent diff.

audienceId.description: The Facebook custom audience this connection delivers to. Required: the transformer throws 'Audience ID is a mandatory field' without it. A Meta audience id is a numeric string, so the pattern refuses an empty or whitespace-only value and a name typed in by mistake, which would otherwise pass create and fail every record at the first sync.

isHashRequired.description: Required, and no default: an omitted value is read as `false`, and `processAudienceRecord` then throws a hashing-consistency error on raw warehouse values. The destination's own configSchema defaults it to true, but nothing applies that default to the per-connection block, so the caller has to say which it wants. Warehouse columns are normally raw, which makes `true` the usual answer.

isRaw.description: Whether the incoming identifier values are already hashed. Read as false when omitted.

disableFormat.description: Skips the transformer's normalisation of identifier values before hashing. Read as false when omitted.

type.description: data_source.type on the Facebook payload. Omitted, nothing is sent; the webapp writes FILE_IMPORTED, so a connection meant to match one made in the dashboard has to set it.

subType.description: data_source.sub_type on the Facebook payload. Enumerated rather than left a free string because the transformer forwards whatever it is given: 'MULTI_HASH' for 'MULTI_HASHES' would be accepted here and then rejected by Meta. The list is copied from this destination's own configSchema and a test asserts the two stay identical. The webapp writes MULTI_HASHES.
